protocol.name: treeland_cross_subsurface_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
Extends wl_subcompositor to support sub-surface relationships between surfaces belonging to different client connections.
In wl_subcompositor both the parent surface and sibling surfaces must be local wl_surface objects from the same client. This protocol removes that restriction by using token-based identifiers exchanged out-of-band:
1. A client exports a wl_surface and receives a surface_token.
2. Another client exports their own wl_surface and then calls create_remote_subsurface with the parent's surface_token, attaching their surface as a child.
All sub-surface semantics follow the wl_subcompositor specification unless explicitly noted in this document. Cross-process sub-surfaces are always in desynchronized mode; synchronized mode is not supported.
The compositor must restrict binding to trusted clients. A client that obtains a surface_token must only share it with other trusted clients through a secure mechanism; the compositor does not disclose tokens to other clients.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_subsurface_manager_v1
interface.description: Global factory object for exporting surfaces.

entry.name: bad_surface
entry.summary: the wl_surface has already been exported through this manager

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind from the sub-surface manager interface

request.description: Informs the server that the client will not use this protocol object anymore. This does not affect any other objects, treeland_exported_surface_v1 and treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 objects included.

request.name: export_surface

description.summary: register a surface for cross-process sub-surface use

request.description:
Register surface as addressable by token, receiving a treeland_exported_surface_v1. Upon success the compositor emits the surface_token event.
The surface must not have been previously exported through this manager. A surface may carry both an xdg_toplevel (or any other) role and an export; the export only marks it as addressable by token.

interface.name: treeland_exported_surface_v1

description.summary: an exported surface, addressable by token

interface.description:
Represents a wl_surface registered for cross-process sub-surface use. The surface may act as a parent (when another client attaches to it) or as a child (when create_remote_subsurface is called on it). A surface can have at most one parent via this protocol.
Destroying this object revokes the surface_token; subsequent use of the token in create_remote_subsurface results in a bad_parent_token error and in place_above or place_below results in a bad_sibling error. Existing parent-child relationships and treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 objects are not affected.

entry.name: bad_surface
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has an incompatible role

entry.name: bad_parent_token
entry.summary: parent_token does not identify a live exported surface

entry.name: cyclic_parent
entry.summary: parent_token would introduce a cycle in the sub-surface tree

request.name: destroy
request.description:
The surface_token is revoked. Existing parent-child relationships and treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 objects are not affected.
The client must destroy this object before destroying the associated wl_surface.

request.name: create_remote_subsurface

description.summary: attach this surface as a child to a remote parent

request.description:
Attach the exported surface to the parent identified by parent_token, turning it into a cross-process sub-surface.
The surface must not already carry a wl_subsurface role, a treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 role, or already have a parent via a previous create_remote_subsurface call.
The parent_token must be a valid surface_token from a live treeland_exported_surface_v1 object. Providing an unknown or already-destroyed parent_token, or an empty string, results in a bad_parent_token error. The compositor should also reject parent_token values that refer to surfaces belonging to untrusted clients.
The compositor must detect cycles in the sub-surface tree. The parent_token must not equal this surface's own surface_token (self-loop), and must not refer to any surface that is a descendant of this surface in the sub-surface tree (indirect cycle). A cyclic_parent error is raised for both cases.
Adding the sub-surface to a parent is double-buffered on the parent.
Upon success the compositor creates the sub-surface relationship.

arg.name: parent_token
arg.summary: surface_token of the parent, obtained via export

event.name: surface_token
event.description: Emitted immediately after export_surface. The value is a unique string of at most 128 characters, cryptographically safe. The client shares this token with other clients so they can create cross-process sub-surfaces or reference this surface as a sibling.

interface.name: treeland_remote_subsurface_v1

description.summary: cross-process sub-surface interface to a wl_surface

interface.description:
An additional interface to a wl_surface object, which has been made a sub-surface of a parent belonging to a different client connection. A sub-surface has one parent surface. A sub-surface's size and position are not limited to that of the parent. Particularly, a sub-surface is not automatically clipped to its parent's area.
Mapping follows the standard sub-surface rules: mapped when both a non-NULL buffer is applied and the parent is mapped; hidden when the parent is hidden or a NULL buffer is applied; recursive through the tree of surfaces.
The parent is identified at creation time and cannot be changed. place_above and place_below accept a token (string) instead of a wl_surface proxy; see the request documentation for valid values.
Cross-process sub-surfaces are always in desynchronized mode: wl_surface.commit applies the pending state directly. Calling wl_surface.commit on the parent has no effect on the sub-surface's state.
A sub-surface never has the keyboard focus of any seat. The wl_surface.offset request is ignored; clients must use set_position instead.

entry.name: bad_sibling
entry.summary: sibling_token does not identify a valid sibling under the same parent, or the parent itself

request.name: destroy
request.description: Removes the sub-surface association and unmaps the wl_surface immediately.

request.name: set_position
request.description: Schedules a position change relative to the parent surface coordinate system. Coordinates are not restricted to the parent area; negative values are allowed. Double-buffered on the parent; replaces any previous pending position. Initial position is 0, 0.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x coordinate in the parent surface local coordinate system

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y coordinate in the parent surface local coordinate system

request.name: place_above
request.description:
Places this sub-surface just above the reference identified by sibling_token, changing the z-order. Z-order is double-buffered on the parent surface. A new sub-surface is initially added at the top.
Valid sibling_token values:
- The surface_token of the parent exported surface.
- The surface_token of any sibling cross-process sub-surface under the same parent, shared via out-of-band communication.
- An empty string (""), a sentinel meaning "place at the very top of the sibling stack".
Using an unrecognized token results in a bad_sibling protocol error.

arg.name: sibling_token
arg.summary: a surface_token or empty string for top

request.name: place_below
request.description: Places this sub-surface just below the reference identified by sibling_token. The same values are accepted as in place_above, except that the empty string sentinel is not valid and will result in a bad_sibling protocol error.
